title: PR review postmortem and follow-ups (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context
---
Quick personal write-up for PR #4823 (kv-cache concurrency fix + small refactor). Kept this as a scratchpad during review and after merge to capture follow-ups, things I wanted but didn't ask for, and quick commands to reproduce perf numbers. Mostly notes to self — messy.

Summary of what PR changed
- Introduced a lightweight sharded lock for KV cache write path (ShardLock) to reduce global lock contention.
- Moved cache eviction logic out of the hot path into an async background worker (cache_maintenance).
- Small API surface change: Cache::get_or_insert -> Cache::fetch_or_populate (semantic change around race handling).
- Added unit tests but minimal integration perf tests (TODO).

Why I flagged this in review
- Locking semantics: the new ShardLock implementation is subtle. It uses per-shard mutex + a global epoch counter to coordinate evictions. I wanted an explicit docblock explaining ordering/invariants — not present. Risk: future change could drop global epoch update and introduce stale reads.
- API rename/unexpected semantic change: fetch_or_populate now returns a Result<(Entry, Source), Error> where Source indicates origin (cache/hot-populated). Call sites assume prior get_or_insert always returned the cached reference; some usage patterns may now trigger duplicate population attempts (observed in PR CI flakiness).
- Background worker scheduling: default schedule is 5s interval — might be too aggressive for tiny pods, causing CPU spikes in low-traffic scenarios.

Immediate TODOs (post-merge)
- [ ] Add docstring/comments for ShardLock invariants and removal conditions. (owner: jordan / priority: high)
- [ ] Add an integration perf test that simulates 50k concurrent kv gets with mixed read/write to replicate contention. (owner: priya / priority: high)
- [ ] Audit importers of Cache::get_or_insert across repo and update call sites to properly handle the new Result/Source union. Grep: `get_or_insert\b` and `fetch_or_populate\b`. (owner: ethan / priority: medium)
- [ ] Expose config knobs for cache_maintenance.interval and default to 15s for small-instance profiles. (owner: product? / priority: low)
- [ ] Add canary rollout notes for dedicated pool with 10% traffic and fallback policy to previous model if latency regresses > 10ms. (owner: eng-ops / priority: medium)

Notes I left inline as code comments (things I care about but didn't block on)
- Consider switching the epoch increment from a CAS loop to an overflowing u64 increment (current CAS loop could theoretically starve under pathological update patterns).
- The per-shard lock uses Mutex<T> — maybe a parking_lot::Mutex would be faster and lower overhead in hot paths. Benchmark before swapping.
- Unit test coverage: missing a test for concurrent eviction + read in the same microsecond window (race condition that could return stale pointer).

Repro commands / quick perf checks
- Local perf harness (run from repo root):
  - `cargo run -p kv-bench --release -- --concurrency 500 --reads 0.9 --requests 50000`
  - Baseline (pre-PR): ~1300 reqs/sec median latency 8ms. Post-PR (local) observed ~1600 reqs/sec median 6ms. Need CI-scale tests though.
- Capture flamegraph locally (use brewed perf):
  - `RUSTFLAGS=\"-Cinstrument-coverage\" cargo build --release && target/release/kv-bench --...`
  - `cargo flamegraph --bin kv-bench --release -- --concurrency 500`

Follow-up discussion points for sync meeting
- Rollout strategy: how long to keep old version as fallback? request 48h of canary traffic then evaluate. Also need automated alert: 95th latency up > 12ms triggers rollback.
- Telemetry: we currently emit metrics `kv.cache.hit_ratio` and `kv.cache.evictions_total`. Add `kv.cache.shard_lock_wait_ms` to measure contention. (owner: observability)
- API ergonomics: is Source enum useful long-term? Might be cleaner to have a simple boolean + detailed tracing event on population path.

Unresolved questions
- Did we change semantics for callers who rely on reference stability inside cache entries? I left TODO to scan for `&Entry` lifetime assumptions.
- Are any external plugins (older forks) calling internal Cache:: internals via pub(crate) shims? Might break them. Need to search our internal bazel packages and partner repos.

Random notes / brain dump (small snippets saved during review)
- If we see read-heavy traffic, the background eviction worker could be relaxed to run less frequently but do larger batch evictions. Might improve tail latencies.
- For small instances, a single-shard cache with no background worker might be ok — add profile named `tiny-pod` to configs.
- On the retry semantics: fetch_or_populate currently retries population up to 3x on transient errors. Good, but should expose as config and surface in traces.

Patch ideas that I didn't write (future refactors)
1) ShardLock -> Rcu-style readers/writer: implement optimistic read path with epoch checks, fallback to write lock only on eviction. Would reduce contention for reads to zero. Big change, needs proof-of-concept.
2) Cache eviction: move to a token-bucket paced evictor rather than fixed-interval to smooth CPU spikes.
3) Introduce a small structured event `cache_population` with fields (key, duration_ms, source, success) for tracing + histogram.

Code snippets I left in comments (quick cleanup later)
- Grep helper: `rg "\\bget_or_insert\\b|\\bfetch_or_populate\\b" -S --hidden --glob '!target'`
- Replace sites: `git grep -n "get_or_insert(" | awk -F: '{print $1":"$2}' | xargs -I {} sed -n "{}p"`

Personal checklist before I mark this final
- [x] Confirm no obvious security issues (no new public endpoints, config flags default to safe values).
- [ ] Run full integration suite with 3 dedicated pods under load (blocked on infra window).
- [ ] Add docs + short design note in confluence: /confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=98765432 (TODO create)

Slack notes to drop after merge (short messages)
- "Merged #4823 — reduces KV cache contention. Please watch kv.cache.shard_lock_wait_ms and alert if 95p > 50ms. Rolling out canary 10%."
- If rollback needed: "Rolling back #4823 due to latency regression — fallback traffic to v1 instances. Will post postmortem."

Final raw thoughts
- Overall change looks good and moves the needle on throughput. My main worry is long-term maintenance complexity of ShardLock invariants. Need design note and at least one perf harness in CI before we feel comfortable toggling this on for all clusters.

End of scratchpad. Will move items into proper tickets and tidy up comments once infra slot opens.

-- jordan
